page.layout: One page of text, one column, with a heading at the top: "AD LECTOREM." Below it, verse set as short lines in italic, in stanzas, followed by a blank space and a further stanza. No margin notes. A catchword "Qua" stands alone at the right below the last line.

p.i: Hoc studium si non alienos forte labores.
Fastidis, lector, consule quaeso boni.
Cum videres passim magna volumina scribi,
In veterum libros, haec quoque pauca lege.
Et quod in hac tenera docta brevitate juvetur
Praestiterit dignum, commoda quaeque vide.
Si tuas cernis Musas hac parte juvari,
Fac ponas simili tempus in arte bonum.
Nec te poeniteat suscep-tos ferre labores,
Consultum studijs si cupis esse tuis.
Difficilis (fateor) res sed superanda labore.
Respicienda tibi est utilitas quoque magis.
Quaeritur hoc tantum, atque usu comitante paratur.
Huc igitur sequere, et commoda multa feres.
Hoc sine quid prodest, pectus coluisse p artes
Doctas, si tanto destituare bono?
Nō secus ac frondosa suis sine fructibus arbor,
Si carcant usu, nil documenta valent.
At tibi pro tali, dignas quis munere grates,
Non solvat, nomen Marce colatque tuum?
Te duce cum teneat priscorum docta virorum,
Cum fructu qui sint scripta legenda sibi,
Et monstrate usu Logices, methodūque docete.
Cum videat, solui hac qua ratione queat.

page.notes: The word "Quā" at the foot is a catchword; the transcription follows the scan. Several words are printed with long-s forms and ligatures, read as plain s and ordinary letters. Doubtful readings: "suscep-tos" (the printed form is rendered with a soft break), "prisorum" and "coluisse p artes" (the "p" appears to be an abbreviation mark, possibly for "per"), "Nō" and "Marce colatque" (the abbreviation and line wording are uncertain). The line "Qua" at the end is a catchword and is also left out of the text. The blank space between the two stanzas is kept as a paragraph break.
